## New

- PC: one mouse and keyboard for two PCs (Windows and macOS). On a linked PC's page, under **Mouse & keyboard**, pick where its screen is; push the pointer past that edge and the mouse and keyboard go over, and come back the same way. Whichever PC's own mouse moves takes the pointer, so the mouse can be plugged into either one. Between a PC and a Mac, Ctrl and ⌘ trade places. **Ctrl+Alt+Esc** (Ctrl+⌥+Esc on a Mac) brings a stuck pointer back. A Mac needs Dotlink allowed under Accessibility.
- PC: **Pointer speed** for the shared mouse on each PC, from 0.5× to 2×.
- PC: more than two PCs can share the mouse, each placed next to its neighbours: the pointer goes on from one to the next.
- PC: with Clipboard sync on, files and folders copied in Explorer or Finder can be pasted on the other PC. Big copies come when the pointer goes over or when you paste, and a notification says when they're on their way and when they're ready.

## Fixes

- Phone: dragging along the tab bar or a two-way switch ticks at each tab on every phone.
